Chronic knee pain seems like a fact of life as we get older. According to some estimates, roughly a quarter of people living in the United States currently suffer from it. If you’ve experienced it, you know how dramatically it can reduce your quality of life, transforming even a mundane chore into an excruciating ordeal. The treatments—painkillers, physical therapy, and at-home exercises—come with their own side effects and drawbacks. Now, according to a study in the journal Nutrients, a fiber supplement could offer at least a little relief.The study, conducted by medical researchers from the University of Nottingham, focused on inulin (not insulin).
